# Blender on Voyager GPUs

Quick stills and previews render fine locally. Slow Cycles work (animations, high sample counts,
heavy volumes, many takes) is where a machine pays off. To decide locally, time one frame at reduced
resolution or samples and scale it. Once a machine is approved, skip local timing: the render
script reports `seconds_per_frame` (without the warm-up frame). Multiply by the frame count, divide
by the GPUs, add a few minutes for startup and transfer, and price it with `credits_per_minute`
from offers for that GPU count.

The default image has `blender` on PATH; `voyager machine images` lists its version. A scene saved
by a newer Blender may not open, so check `blender --version` with a short exec. Cycles and EEVEE
both run on the default card; EEVEE draws on one GPU.

## Pack the scene

Send one self-contained copy; the original stays untouched:

```sh
blender -b --factory-startup scene.blend --python <this skill>/scripts/pack_scene.py -- --out render/scene.blend --make-local
```

It packs images, fonts, sounds and volumes; `--make-local` copies linked library data in.
`PACK_SCENE_JSON` lists what still needs attention: `external` files (image sequences, movies,
caches, bakes) to push with the same relative paths (`outside: true`: move them under `render/`
first); `missing` files to fix; `unbaked` simulations to bake first, since a split frame range
simulates from each slice's start; and `scripted_drivers`, which run only with `-y` before the
scene path.

## Render

`<this skill>/scripts/blender_render.py` enables OptiX (CUDA fallback) on every GPU the process
sees, refuses to fall back to the CPU, resumes, and reports progress. Copy it into `render/`, push
`render` (plus external paths) and run it detached from `/project`:

```sh
voyager machine sync push ocean --include render
voyager machine exec ocean --detach --request-id hero-1 --cwd /project -- blender -b -q --factory-startup render/scene.blend --python render/blender_render.py -- --frames 1-240 --out /project/out/hero --engine cycles
```

It writes `out/hero/0001.png…` and keeps `out/hero-render-1-240.json` (`done`, `total`,
`eta_seconds`, device names, seconds per frame, `fps`) current. Each frame logs
`BLENDER_RENDER_FRAME <frame> <seconds> <done>/<total> eta <s>s`, so `logs` with a small
`tailBytes` reads progress. Check that `BLENDER_RENDER_DEVICE` names the GPU and the first frames
appear. `--samples N` overrides the scene. `--resume` keeps finished frames: after a lost,
cancelled or paused job, run the same command again with `--resume`.

Cycles denoises with OpenImageDenoise on the GPU by default: the OptiX denoiser fails on the
Blackwell cards ("Failed to create OptiX denoiser") although OptiX rendering works. A scene script
of your own that sets `cycles.denoiser = "OPTIX"` hits the same error; `"OPENIMAGEDENOISE"` with
`cycles.denoising_use_gpu = True` is the fix. `--denoiser optix` (other cards) or `--denoiser scene`
(keep the scene's choice) override it.

A still or a few frames: one exec; Cycles uses every GPU it sees. An animation or other work that
splits into chunks: [gpujob](fanout.md) keeps every GPU busy and retries failed chunks.

## Encode and finish

Encode on the machine and pull one file. Choose by what comes next:

- A finished animation: H.264 MP4 (below).
- More grading or editing: ProRes 422 HQ (`-c:v prores_ks -profile:v hq -pix_fmt yuv422p10le
hero.mov`; `-profile:v 4444 -pix_fmt yuva444p10le` keeps alpha) or HEVC 10-bit
  (`-c:v hevc_nvenc -preset p7 -cq 16 -b:v 0 -pix_fmt p010le -tag:v hvc1`).
- The user wants the frames, or a frame-level fix: pull `out/hero` and run
  `voyager blender finalize out/hero --fps <fps>`.
- A re-encode looks likely: keep the frames on the machine, or snapshot it before release.

From `/project/out`, with the summary's `fps` and first frame (`--shell`; NVENC, else libx264):

```sh
q="-framerate 24 -start_number 1 -i hero/%04d.png -vf scale=out_color_matrix=bt709,setparams=colorspace=bt709:color_primaries=bt709:color_trc=bt709 -pix_fmt yuv420p -movflags +faststart -y"
ffmpeg $q -c:v h264_nvenc -preset p7 -profile:v high -rc vbr -cq 18 -b:v 0 hero.mp4 || ffmpeg $q -c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 16 hero.mp4
```

Look at it with `inspect`, pull just that file, then run
`voyager blender finalize out/hero.mp4 --fps <fps> --frame-count <frames> --start-frame <first> --machine <name>`.
It decodes the whole video, checks frame count and duration, and writes the `.blender.json` the
canvas reads, recording the remote encode. Use finalize rather than `ingest` for Blender
animations; a single still needs neither.

# Chunked jobs and fan-out

Work that splits into independent chunks (frames, tiles, shots, seeds) fits `gpujob.py`: it keeps
every GPU on a machine busy, commits a chunk only once all its files exist, retries a failed chunk
on another GPU, and after a cancel, pause, lost job or new GPU count the same command resumes.
Python 3.10+, standard library only.

## One machine

Copy `<this skill>/scripts/gpujob.py` and `gpujob_core.py` into `render/` with a `render/job.json`,
push `render`, and run `python3 render/gpujob.py run render/job.json` as one detached exec:

```json
{
  "name": "hero",
  "workdir": "/project",
  "credits_per_gpu_minute": 6.6,
  "stages": [
    {
      "name": "render",
      "range": [1, 240],
      "chunk": 4,
      "out": "out/hero",
      "outputs": "{frame:04d}.png",
      "cmd": [
        "blender",
        "-b",
        "-q",
        "--factory-startup",
        "render/scene.blend",
        "--python",
        "render/blender_render.py",
        "--",
        "--frames",
        "{start}-{end}",
        "--out",
        "{tmp}",
        "--resume"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

`credits_per_gpu_minute` is `credits_per_minute` from offers with `gpus: 1` for the card; it only
feeds the credit figures. `{start}`, `{end}`, `{tmp}` and `{frame}` are filled per chunk.

- Log lines like `GPUJOB progress 42% 101/240 frames eta 190s 61 credits` feed the activity tray.
- `python3 render/gpujob.py status /project/.gpujob/hero` answers "how long left?" in one short exec;
  `report` gives GPU time, idle time and credits at the end.
- `estimate --pilot` renders a few real chunks (kept) and prices 1–4 GPUs and several machines as a
  low–high range; quote the range. `--pilot-seconds S` estimates from a known chunk time.
- A `"kind": "sequential"` stage (a simulation) can stream into a render stage that reads it.

## Several machines

`gpujob_fanout.py` runs one job over several machines from this computer: it leases them, starts
work on the first that is ready, hands work from slow or lost machines to others, pulls
hash-verified outputs home as they finish, and releases everything at the end. Use it when one
machine's GPUs aren't enough, or when a single 4-GPU machine is slow to start. Run it as a tracked
local job so it outlives the turn and wakes the conversation when it ends:

```sh
voyager jobs run --title "Render hero" -- python3 <this skill>/scripts/gpujob_fanout.py fanout render/job.json --machines 2 --gpus-per-machine 4 --push render
```

`--cpu` and `--ram-gib` shape each machine, `--gpu-type` picks the card, and `--idle-s` (default 900) lets a machine release itself if the coordinator stops. Without `credits_per_gpu_minute` it
prices the card from current offers, and its end line and `.gpujob-fanout-report.json` report the
credits the machines actually spent. Running the same command again resumes and releases any
machines a killed run left behind.

# Recovery and preservation

## Reconnect

Save the machine name and `job_id` from exec. After a disconnect or a lost context, `list` shows
your machines, `jobs` a machine's jobs, and `job status` or `logs` (from the last `next_cursor`)
picks the work back up. A foreground exec that outlasts its wait comes back with
`background: true` and keeps running: inspect that job instead of starting it again. A lost or
failed job is evidence to read before retrying; rerun with the same request ID only for the same
operation.

## What each option keeps

Read `capabilities`, a snapshot's `preservation` and the `resume_note` before promising
continuity. Preservation names disk, RAM, processes, GPU state and mounted volumes separately.

- `snapshot` kind `disk`: files and installed packages. Processes restart. A volume mounted at
  `/persist` is kept separately and is not part of a root snapshot.
- `pause` mode `checkpoint`: runs an optional `hookArgv` save step, stops jobs, takes a disk
  snapshot and releases the GPU. On resume, restart the program from its own saved checkpoint.
- `pause` mode `retain`: keeps the live machine and keeps billing. Useful for live state only.
- `resume`: same machine name and ID on a new allocation, from the latest or a named snapshot.
  Reopen connections and restart jobs.
- `fork`: a new, separately billed machine from a snapshot. Keep its outputs apart, and don't
  repeat external side effects (publishing, uploads) from both.

Where a mode isn't supported the API refuses it rather than quietly doing less; tell the user
what is possible instead.

## Release

Release once outputs are home or snapshotted. An uncertain release answer is not proof billing
stopped: check `status` (or `list`) shows it released, and retry with the same request ID. The
project volume is kept unless `keepVolume` is false. Next time, start from the saved snapshot or
volume instead of keeping an idle machine.

## Render errors

`Failed to create OptiX denoiser` in a Blender log: the OptiX denoiser fails on the Blackwell
cards while OptiX rendering works. Rerun with OpenImageDenoise on the GPU (the render script's
default; see [Blender](blender.md)).

"""Render a saved Blender scene's frames headless on every GPU this process can see.

    blender -b -q --factory-startup scene.blend --python blender_render.py -- \\
        --out /project/out/hero [--frames 1-120] [--engine cycles|eevee] [--samples N] \\
        [--percent 100] [--denoiser oidn|optix|scene] [--resume] [--allow-cpu] [--summary path.json]

-q keeps Blender's own per-sample status lines (Blender 4.x prints one per sample) out of the log,
leaving this script's lines, warnings and errors.

Cycles: tries OPTIX, then CUDA (then HIP, Metal, oneAPI), enables every device of the first backend
that has one, sets the scene to GPU and refuses to render on the CPU unless --allow-cpu is given.
With several GPUs visible, Cycles splits each frame across all of them; restrict a process with
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES to run one process per GPU on separate frame ranges. EEVEE needs a graphics
device (EGL) and has no device setting; a software OpenGL renderer is refused after the first frame.

Cycles denoises with OpenImageDenoise, on the GPU where Blender supports it, when the scene has
denoising on: the OptiX denoiser fails to start on Blackwell cards ("Failed to create OptiX
denoiser") although OptiX rendering works. --denoiser optix picks OptiX's, --denoiser scene keeps
the scene's own choice.

Frames are PNGs named ####.png (0001.png …) in --out, the layout `voyager blender finalize` reads.
--frames is START-END or one frame, inclusive; omitted, the scene's own range and step. --resume
keeps frames already in --out and renders only the missing ones, saying how many it kept in one
``BLENDER_RENDER_RESUME <kept>/<total>`` line.

Prints one ``BLENDER_RENDER_DEVICE <backend>: <names>`` line (EEVEE: after its first frame), then
``BLENDER_RENDER_FRAME <frame> <seconds> <done>/<total> eta <seconds>s`` per frame (done counts
kept frames; eta is the median seconds per frame times the frames left), so the last line of a
short log tail is the slice's progress. It keeps a JSON summary (default: beside --out, named
<out>-render-<first>-<last>.json) up to date from the start and after each frame: ``done``,
``total``, ``eta_seconds``, Blender version, engine, device, resolution, samples, ``fps`` as
``voyager blender finalize --fps`` takes it, every rendered frame with its seconds, and the median
seconds per frame (the first frame, which loads the scene and compiles kernels, is left out once
there are more). Finished frames are the only visible PNGs in --out (a frame in progress is a
hidden partial), so counting them reads the progress of every slice rendering into one folder.
Every failure prints ``blender_render: error: ...`` and exits non-zero.
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import statistics
import sys
import time
from fractions import Fraction

import bpy

BACKENDS = ("OPTIX", "CUDA", "HIP", "METAL", "ONEAPI")


class Failure(Exception):
    pass


def arguments():
    argv = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1 :] if "--" in sys.argv else []
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="blender_render.py")
    parser.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="Folder for the PNG frames")
    parser.add_argument("--frames", help="START-END or one frame (default: the scene's range)")
    parser.add_argument("--engine", choices=("cycles", "eevee"), help="Default: the scene's engine")
    parser.add_argument("--samples", type=int, help="Render samples (default: the scene's)")
    parser.add_argument("--percent", type=int, help="Resolution percentage (default: the scene's)")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--denoiser",
        choices=("oidn", "optix", "scene"),
        default="oidn",
        help="Cycles denoiser when the scene denoises (default: oidn, on the GPU)",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--resume", action="store_true", help="Keep frames already in --out")
    parser.add_argument("--allow-cpu", action="store_true", help="Render Cycles on the CPU when no GPU is found")
    parser.add_argument("--summary", help="Summary JSON path")
    return parser.parse_args(argv)


def frame_list(scene, text):
    if not text:
        return list(range(scene.frame_start, scene.frame_end + 1, max(1, scene.frame_step)))
    first, _, last = text.partition("-")
    try:
        start, end = int(first), int(last or first)
    except ValueError:
        raise Failure("--frames %r is not START-END or one frame" % text)
    if end < start:
        raise Failure("--frames %r ends before it starts" % text)
    return list(range(start, end + 1))


def set_engine(scene, engine):
    if engine == "cycles":
        scene.render.engine = "CYCLES"
    elif engine == "eevee":
        # Blender 4.2-4.5 calls it BLENDER_EEVEE_NEXT; 5.x BLENDER_EEVEE.
        names = {item.identifier for item in bpy.types.RenderSettings.bl_rna.properties["engine"].enum_items}
        scene.render.engine = "BLENDER_EEVEE_NEXT" if "BLENDER_EEVEE_NEXT" in names else "BLENDER_EEVEE"
    if scene.render.engine not in ("CYCLES", "BLENDER_EEVEE", "BLENDER_EEVEE_NEXT"):
        raise Failure("the scene renders with %s; pass --engine cycles or --engine eevee" % scene.render.engine)


def select_gpu(scene, allow_cpu):
    """Factory startup has no compute device preference: enable every device of the best backend."""
    if scene.render.engine != "CYCLES":
        return {"backend": "EEVEE", "devices": []}  # its GPU is known after the first frame
    preferences = bpy.context.preferences.addons["cycles"].preferences
    for backend in BACKENDS:
        try:
            preferences.compute_device_type = backend
        except TypeError:
            continue
        preferences.get_devices()
        devices = [device for device in preferences.devices if device.type == backend]
        if devices:
            for device in preferences.devices:
                device.use = device.type == backend
            scene.cycles.device = "GPU"
            used = [device.name for device in preferences.devices if device.use and device.type == backend]
            if used:
                return {"backend": backend, "devices": used}
    if not allow_cpu:
        raise Failure(
            "Cycles found no GPU (tried %s); nothing was rendered. Check nvidia-smi and CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, "
            "or pass --allow-cpu" % ", ".join(BACKENDS)
        )
    scene.cycles.device = "CPU"
    return {"backend": "CPU", "devices": ["%d threads" % os.cpu_count()]}


def eevee_renderer(allow_cpu):
    """The OpenGL/Vulkan renderer EEVEE drew with; a software one means no graphics device."""
    import gpu

    renderer = "%s (%s)" % (gpu.platform.renderer_get(), gpu.platform.backend_type_get())
    if not allow_cpu and any(word in renderer.lower() for word in ("llvmpipe", "softpipe", "swrast")):
        raise Failure("EEVEE rendered with %s, a software renderer: the machine has no graphics device" % renderer)
    return renderer


def set_denoiser(scene, denoiser, device):
    """OpenImageDenoise by default: the OptiX denoiser fails to start on Blackwell cards."""
    if scene.render.engine != "CYCLES" or denoiser == "scene":
        return
    cycles = scene.cycles
    choices = {item.identifier for item in cycles.bl_rna.properties["denoiser"].enum_items}
    if denoiser == "optix" and "OPTIX" not in choices:
        raise Failure(
            "the OptiX denoiser needs Cycles on an OptiX GPU (device: %s); pass --denoiser oidn" % device["backend"]
        )
    cycles.denoiser = "OPENIMAGEDENOISE" if denoiser == "oidn" else "OPTIX"
    if denoiser == "oidn" and hasattr(cycles, "denoising_use_gpu"):  # Blender 4.1+
        cycles.denoising_use_gpu = device["backend"] != "CPU"


def set_samples(scene, samples):
    if samples is None:
        return
    if samples < 1:
        raise Failure("--samples must be at least 1")
    if scene.render.engine == "CYCLES":
        scene.cycles.samples = samples
    else:
        scene.eevee.taa_render_samples = samples


def frame_rate(render):
    """The scene's rate as `voyager blender finalize --fps` takes it: 24, or 30000/1001."""
    rate = Fraction(render.fps) / Fraction(render.fps_base).limit_denominator(10000)
    return str(rate.numerator) if rate.denominator == 1 else "%d/%d" % (rate.numerator, rate.denominator)


def write_json(path, value):
    temporary = path + ".tmp"
    with open(temporary, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        json.dump(value, handle, indent=2)
    os.replace(temporary, path)


def main():
    options = arguments()
    if not bpy.data.filepath:
        raise Failure("open a saved .blend: blender -b --factory-startup scene.blend --python blender_render.py -- ...")
    scene = bpy.context.scene
    if scene.camera is None:
        raise Failure("scene %r has no active camera" % scene.name)
    frames = frame_list(scene, options.frames)
    set_engine(scene, options.engine)
    device = select_gpu(scene, options.allow_cpu)
    set_denoiser(scene, options.denoiser, device)
    set_samples(scene, options.samples)
    if options.percent is not None:
        scene.render.resolution_percentage = max(1, min(options.percent, 1000))
    render = scene.render
    image = render.image_settings
    if hasattr(image, "media_type"):  # Blender 5.x separates image and video output
        image.media_type = "IMAGE"
    image.file_format = "PNG"
    render.use_file_extension = False
    if render.engine == "CYCLES":
        render.use_persistent_data = True  # keep the scene loaded between frames
    out = os.path.abspath(options.out)
    os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
    summary_path = options.summary or "%s-render-%d-%d.json" % (out.rstrip(os.sep), frames[0], frames[-1])
    percentage = render.resolution_percentage
    summary = {
        "blend": bpy.data.filepath,
        "scene": scene.name,
        "blender": bpy.app.version_string,
        "engine": render.engine,
        "device": device,
        "denoiser": scene.cycles.denoiser if render.engine == "CYCLES" and scene.cycles.use_denoising else None,
        "cuda_visible_devices": os.environ.get("CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES"),
        "resolution": [render.resolution_x * percentage // 100, render.resolution_y * percentage // 100],
        "samples": scene.cycles.samples if render.engine == "CYCLES" else scene.eevee.taa_render_samples,
        "fps": frame_rate(render),
        "out": out,
        "frames_requested": [frames[0], frames[-1]],
        "frames": [],
        "skipped": [],
        "done": 0,
        "total": len(frames),
        "eta_seconds": None,
        "seconds_per_frame": None,
        "seconds_total": 0.0,
        "complete": False,
    }
    if render.engine == "CYCLES":
        print("BLENDER_RENDER_DEVICE %s: %s" % (device["backend"], ", ".join(device["devices"])), flush=True)
    paths = {frame: os.path.join(out, "%04d.png" % frame) for frame in frames}
    if options.resume:
        summary["skipped"] = [
            frame for frame in frames if os.path.isfile(paths[frame]) and os.path.getsize(paths[frame]) > 0
        ]
        print("BLENDER_RENDER_RESUME %d/%d" % (len(summary["skipped"]), len(frames)), flush=True)
    kept = set(summary["skipped"])
    pending = [frame for frame in frames if frame not in kept]
    summary["done"] = len(kept)
    write_json(summary_path, summary)
    started_all = time.monotonic()
    for index, frame in enumerate(pending):
        path = paths[frame]
        scene.frame_set(frame)
        # Written under a hidden name, then renamed: a killed render never leaves a partial frame
        # that --resume or finalize would take for a finished one.
        partial = os.path.join(out, ".%04d.partial.png" % frame)
        render.filepath = partial
        started = time.monotonic()
        bpy.ops.render.render(write_still=True, scene=scene.name)
        seconds = time.monotonic() - started
        if not os.path.isfile(partial):
            raise Failure("frame %d was not written to %s" % (frame, partial))
        os.replace(partial, path)
        if render.engine != "CYCLES" and not device["devices"]:
            device["devices"] = [eevee_renderer(options.allow_cpu)]
            print("BLENDER_RENDER_DEVICE EEVEE: %s" % device["devices"][0], flush=True)
        summary["frames"].append({"frame": frame, "seconds": round(seconds, 3), "path": path})
        timed = [entry["seconds"] for entry in summary["frames"]]
        summary["seconds_per_frame"] = round(statistics.median(timed[1:] if len(timed) > 1 else timed), 3)
        summary["seconds_total"] = round(time.monotonic() - started_all, 3)
        summary["done"] = len(kept) + index + 1
        summary["eta_seconds"] = round(summary["seconds_per_frame"] * (len(pending) - index - 1))
        write_json(summary_path, summary)
        print(
            "BLENDER_RENDER_FRAME %d %.3f %d/%d eta %ds"
            % (frame, seconds, summary["done"], len(frames), summary["eta_seconds"]),
            flush=True,
        )
    summary["seconds_total"] = round(time.monotonic() - started_all, 3)
    summary["eta_seconds"] = 0
    summary["complete"] = True
    write_json(summary_path, summary)
    print("BLENDER_RENDER_SUMMARY %s" % summary_path, flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        main()
    except Failure as error:
        print("blender_render: error: %s" % error, file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
        sys.exit(2)
    except Exception as error:  # a render or I/O failure: never exit 0 with frames missing
        print("blender_render: error: %s: %s" % (type(error).__name__, error), file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
        sys.exit(1)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""gpujob: heavy GPU work in chunks over every GPU of a machine. Each chunk is committed atomically as it finishes;
re-running the same command resumes; progress, ETA and credits are GPUJOB lines on stdout.

  gpujob.py run job.json [--state DIR] [--gpus 0,1] [--only IDS|@file] [--stages a,b] [--unquarantine]
  gpujob.py status STATE [--json] [--chunks]       gpujob.py report STATE [--json]
  gpujob.py estimate job.json [--pilot-seconds S | --pilot]    gpujob.py harvest STATE --to DIR
Needs gpujob_core.py beside it; several machines: gpujob_fanout.py. Python >= 3.10, stdlib only.
`run` exits 0 when every chunk is committed, 1 when chunks failed every retry (a re-run retries them), 75 when stopped
by SIGTERM/SIGINT (a re-run resumes), 3 when another runner holds the state, 2 on a bad job.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse, glob as globmod, json, os, re, shutil, signal, statistics, subprocess, sys, time, uuid

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from gpujob_core import (HOST, LEASES, POLL, Job, Stage, State, Worker, die_with_parent,
                         fmt_s, fsync_dir, kill_env, now, out, quiet, read_json, read_jsonl, rm, sha256_file, tail,
                         try_lock, unit_files, write_json)

ME = os.path.abspath(__file__)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- run (supervisor)
def detect_gpus(spec_gpus, arg):
    if arg:
        return [g.strip() for g in arg.split(",") if g.strip()]
    if spec_gpus not in (None, "all"):
        return [str(g) for g in spec_gpus] if isinstance(spec_gpus, list) else [str(i) for i in range(int(spec_gpus))]
    if os.environ.get("GPUJOB_GPUS"):
        return os.environ["GPUJOB_GPUS"].split(",")
    r = quiet(subprocess.run, ["nvidia-smi", "-L"], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)
    n = len([l for l in r.stdout.splitlines() if l.startswith("GPU ")]) if r else 0
    cvd = os.environ.get("CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES")
    return [str(i) for i in range(n)] if n else cvd.split(",") if cvd else ["0"]


def parse_only(v):
    if v.startswith("@"):
        with open(v[1:]) as f:
            v = f.read()
    return {x for x in re.split(r"[\s,]+", v) if x}


def summarize(S, sc=None, elapsed=0.0, base=None, gpus=None, workers=None):
    """The progress record (also `status --json`): small, whole-job first."""
    sc, job, base, gpus = sc or S.scan(), S.job, base or {}, gpus or S.run.get("gpus", [])
    stages, busy, retries, tot_u, done_u, eta, seq_eta = {}, 0.0, 0, 0, 0, 0.0, {}
    q = S.quarantined()
    active = max(1, len([g for g in gpus if g not in q]))
    for st in job.stages:
        r, sel = sc[st.name], S.selected(st)
        secs = [(S.done(st.name, c) or {}).get("seconds", 0) for c in r["done"]]
        busy += sum(secs)
        for cid in r["fail_ids"] & set(sel):
            fl = S.fails(st.name, cid)
            busy, retries = busy + sum(f.get("seconds", 0) for f in fl), retries + len(fl)
        if st.kind == "chunks":
            size = lambda cs: sum(st.chunks[c][1] - st.chunks[c][0] + 1 for c in cs)
            u_tot, u_done = size(sel), size(r["done"])
            left, med = len(sel) - len(r["done"]) - len(r["failed"]), statistics.median(secs) if secs else None
            seq_busy = any(sc[s.name]["leased"] or sc[s.name]["ready"] for s in job.stages if s.kind == "sequential")
            st_eta = med * -(-left // max(1, active - (seq_busy and active > 1))) if med is not None else None
            up = seq_eta.get((st.after or {}).get("stage"))
            if up is not None and med:
                st_eta = max(st_eta or 0, up + med)  # streaming: can't finish before its upstream
        else:
            units = S.units(st)
            u_tot = st.total_units if sel else 0
            u_done = u_tot if r["done"] else min(len(units), u_tot)
            st_eta = 0.0 if r["done"] or not sel else None
            mt = sorted(map(os.path.getmtime, unit_files(st.out, st.unit_glob)))[-20:] if not r["done"] else []
            if len(mt) >= 2 and mt[-1] > mt[0]:
                st_eta = (u_tot - u_done) * (mt[-1] - mt[0]) / (len(mt) - 1)
            seq_eta[st.name] = st_eta
        tot_u, done_u = tot_u + u_tot, done_u + u_done
        eta = None if eta is None or (st_eta is None and u_done < u_tot) else max(eta, st_eta or 0)
        stages[st.name] = dict(kind=st.kind, unit=st.unit_label, done_units=u_done, total_units=u_tot,
                               done_chunks=len(r["done"]), total_chunks=len(sel), running=len(r["leased"]),
                               failed_chunks=len(r["failed"]), waiting=len(r["waiting"]),
                               eta_s=None if st_eta is None else round(st_eta, 1))
        for cid in r["leased"]:  # in-flight time
            busy += max(0.0, now() - ((S.lease(st.name, cid) or {}).get("t") or now()))
    billed, rate = base.get("billed_gpu_seconds", 0.0) + elapsed * len(gpus), job.rate
    complete = all(s["done_chunks"] == s["total_chunks"] for s in stages.values())
    pct = 100 if complete else min(99, int(100 * done_u / tot_u) if tot_u else 0)
    return dict(job=job.name, percent=pct, done_units=done_u, total_units=tot_u, complete=complete, stages=stages,
                eta_s=None if eta is None else round(eta, 1), gpus=gpus, quarantined=sorted(q), retries=retries,
                gpu_seconds_busy=round(busy, 1), billed_gpu_seconds=round(billed, 1), credits_so_far=round(billed * rate, 1),
                wall_s=round(base.get("wall_s", 0.0) + elapsed, 1), credits_per_gpu_minute=job.rate * 60,
                credits_projected=None if eta is None else round((billed + eta * len(gpus)) * rate, 1),
                workers=workers or {}, t=round(now(), 1), run_id=S.run.get("run_id"))


def progress_line(p):
    """`GPUJOB progress NN% a/b frames eta Ns N credits ...`: the whole-job percent leads (a progress tray takes it)."""
    ss = [s for s in p["stages"].values() if s["total_units"]]
    main = ss[-1] if ss else {"done_units": 0, "total_units": 0, "unit": "units"}
    rest = " ".join(f"{n} {s['done_units']}/{s['total_units']}" for n, s in p["stages"].items()
                    if s is not main and s["total_units"])
    busy = sum(1 for w in p["workers"].values() if w.get("state") == "busy")
    fails = sum(s["failed_chunks"] for s in p["stages"].values())
    return (f"GPUJOB progress {p['percent']}% {main['done_units']}/{main['total_units']} {main['unit']} eta "
            f"{'?' if p['eta_s'] is None else str(int(p['eta_s'])) + 's'} {p['credits_so_far']:.0f} credits"
            + (f" | {rest}" if rest else "") + f" | gpus {busy}/{len(p['gpus']) - len(p['quarantined'])} busy"
            + (f" quarantined {','.join(p['quarantined'])}" if p["quarantined"] else "")
            + (f" | retries {p['retries']}" if p["retries"] else "") + (f" | failed {fails}" if fails else "")
            + (f" | projected {p['credits_projected']:.0f} credits" if p.get("credits_projected") is not None else ""))


def cmd_run(a):
    job = Job.load(a.job)
    root = os.path.abspath(a.state or os.path.join(job.workdir, ".gpujob", job.name))
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(root, "chunks"), exist_ok=True)
    lockf = open(os.path.join(root, "run.lock"), "w")
    if not try_lock(lockf):
        out(f"GPUJOB error another runner is active on {root}")
        return 3
    for d in (read_json(os.path.join(root, "job.json")) or {}).get("stages", []):  # layout can't change under work
        if d["name"] in job.by and Stage(d, job.workdir, 0).layout() != job.by[d["name"]].layout() \
                and globmod.glob(os.path.join(root, "chunks", d["name"], "*.done")):
            out(f"GPUJOB error stage {d['name']} changed its chunks/out since the last run; use a new --state")
            return 2
    write_json(os.path.join(root, "job.json"), dict(job.spec, workdir=job.workdir))
    for pid in kill_env("GPUJOB_STATE", root):  # we hold the lock: anything still running here is an orphan
        out(f"GPUJOB event killed_orphan pid={pid}")
    # ...and every claim left is a dead run's, even one from another hostname (a replaced container)
    stale = [f for x in LEASES for f in globmod.glob(os.path.join(root, "chunks", "*", "*." + x))]
    [rm(f) for f in stale]
    if stale:
        out(f"GPUJOB reclaimed {len(stale)} leases")
    # finished chunks' attempt folders go; others keep their outputs for the next attempt to carry over
    [rm(f) for st in job.stages for c in (os.listdir(os.path.join(root, "chunks", st.name))
     if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(root, "chunks", st.name)) else []) if c.endswith(".done")
     for f in globmod.glob(os.path.join(st.out, ".tmp", c[:-5] + ".*"))]
    os.environ["GPUJOB_HOSTID"] = HOST  # workers share the runner's machine identity
    if a.unquarantine:
        [rm(f) for f in globmod.glob(os.path.join(root, "gpus", "*.quarantined"))]
    gpus = detect_gpus(job.spec.get("gpus"), a.gpus)
    prev = read_json(os.path.join(root, "progress.json"), {})
    base = {k: prev.get(k, 0.0) for k in ("billed_gpu_seconds", "wall_s")}
    run = dict(run_id=uuid.uuid4().hex[:12], gpus=gpus, started=now(), pid=os.getpid(), host=HOST,
               only=sorted(parse_only(a.only)) if a.only else None, stages=a.stages.split(",") if a.stages else None,
               partition=[int(x) for x in a.partition.split("/")] if a.partition else None)
    write_json(os.path.join(root, "run.json"), run)
    S = State(root, job)
    S.event("run_start", gpus=gpus, run_id=run["run_id"])
    q = S.quarantined()
    if q:
        out(f"GPUJOB event quarantined_gpus_skipped {','.join(sorted(q))} (use --unquarantine to retry them)")
    stopping, procs, deaths = {}, {}, {g: [] for g in gpus}
    for sig in (signal.SIGTERM, signal.SIGINT):
        signal.signal(sig, lambda signum, _: stopping.update(sig=signum))

    def spawn(g):
        procs[g] = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, ME, "_worker", root, g], stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                                    stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=open(S.p("worker-stderr.log"), "ab"),
                                    preexec_fn=die_with_parent)
    [spawn(g) for g in gpus if g not in q]
    t0, last_line, last_write, stuck, rc = now(), ("", 0.0), 0.0, 0, None
    out(f"GPUJOB start job={job.name} gpus={','.join(gpus)} state={root} run={run['run_id']}")
    seen_ev = os.path.getsize(S.p("events.jsonl"))
    while True:
        for g, pr in list(procs.items()):  # a dead worker: clean up after it and restart it
            r = pr.poll()
            if r is None:
                continue
            del procs[g]
            wid = f"{HOST}:{pr.pid}:g{g}"
            kill_env("GPUJOB_WORKER", wid)  # its command and grandchildren, if PDEATHSIG missed any
            [rm(f) for x in LEASES for f in globmod.glob(S.p("chunks", "*", "*." + x))
             if (read_json(f) or {}).get("worker") == wid]
            if stopping or g in S.quarantined():
                continue
            deaths[g] = [t for t in deaths[g] if t > now() - 600] + [now()]
            S.event("worker_died", gpu=g, rc=r, worker=wid)
            why = tail(S.p("worker-stderr.log"), 300).strip().splitlines()[-1:] if r > 0 else []  # crash traceback
            out(f"GPUJOB event worker_died gpu={g} rc={r} restarting" + (f" last_error={why[0][:160]}" if why else ""))
            if len(deaths[g]) > 5:
                write_json(S.p("gpus", f"{g}.quarantined"), dict(t=now(), why="worker died >5 times in 10 min"))
                S.event("gpu_quarantined", gpu=g, why="worker keeps dying")
            else:
                spawn(g)
        evline = False  # failures and quarantines as GPUJOB lines, always followed by a progress line
        with open(S.p("events.jsonl"), "rb") as f:
            f.seek(seen_ev)
            chunk = f.read()
        chunk = chunk[:chunk.rfind(b"\n") + 1]
        seen_ev += len(chunk)
        for e in filter(None, (quiet(json.loads, ln) for ln in chunk.splitlines())):
            if e["ev"] == "chunk_carried":
                out(f"GPUJOB carried {e['outputs']} outputs {e['stage']}:{e['chunk']}")
                evline = True
            elif e["ev"] in ("chunk_fail", "gpu_quarantined", "lease_stolen"):
                out(f"GPUJOB event {e['ev']} " + " ".join(f"{k}={str(v).replace(' ', '_')[:80]}" for k, v in e.items()
                    if k in ("stage", "chunk", "gpu", "rc", "why", "attempt") and v not in ("", None)))
                evline = True
        sc, workers = S.scan(), {}
        for st in job.stages:
            for cid in sc[st.name]["leased"]:
                l = S.lease(st.name, cid) or {}
                workers[str(l.get("gpu"))] = dict(state="busy", item=f"{st.name}:{cid}", since=l.get("t"))
        for g in gpus:
            if g in S.quarantined() or g not in workers:
                workers[g] = dict(state="quarantined" if g in S.quarantined() else "idle" if g in procs else "dead")
        p = summarize(S, sc, now() - t0, base, gpus, workers)
        line = progress_line(p)
        stuck = 0 if p["complete"] or any(sc[s]["leased"] or sc[s]["ready"] for s in sc) else stuck + 1
        rc = 0 if p["complete"] else 75 if stopping else 1 if stuck >= 3 or not procs else None
        p["state"] = {None: "running", 0: "done", 75: "stopped", 1: "failed"}[rc]
        if rc is not None or now() - last_write >= 2:
            write_json(S.p("progress.json"), p)
            last_write = now()
        if rc is not None or evline or line != last_line[0] or now() - last_line[1] > 60:
            out(line)
            last_line = (line, now())
        if rc is not None:
            break
        time.sleep(POLL)
    [quiet(pr.send_signal, signal.SIGTERM) for pr in procs.values()]
    deadline = now() + 8  # workers release their claims within 10 s of SIGTERM
    [quiet(pr.wait, timeout=max(0.1, deadline - now())) for pr in procs.values()]
    kill_env("GPUJOB_STATE", root)
    [rm(f) for x in LEASES for f in globmod.glob(S.p("chunks", "*", "*." + x))  # this run's claims only
     if (read_json(f) or {}).get("run_id") == run["run_id"] or str((read_json(f) or {}).get("worker")).startswith(HOST + ":")]
    p = summarize(S, None, now() - t0, base, gpus, {})
    p["state"] = {0: "done", 75: "stopped"}.get(rc, "failed")
    write_json(S.p("progress.json"), p)
    S.event("run_end", rc=rc, run_id=run["run_id"], seconds=round(now() - t0, 3))
    for st in job.stages if rc == 1 else []:
        for cid in S.scan()[st.name]["failed"][:10]:
            f = S.fails(st.name, cid)[-1]
            out(f"GPUJOB failed {st.name}:{cid} rc={f.get('rc')} {f.get('why', '')} log={f.get('log')}")
    out(f"GPUJOB end {p['state']} {p['percent']}% wall {fmt_s(now() - t0)} gpu_busy {fmt_s(p['gpu_seconds_busy'])} "
        f"{p['credits_so_far']:.0f} credits exit={rc}")
    return rc


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- status, report
def cmd_status(a):
    S = State(a.state)
    p, prev = summarize(S), read_json(S.p("progress.json"), {})
    with open(S.p("run.lock"), "a") as lf:
        running = not try_lock(lf)
    p.update(running=running, state="running" if running else "done" if p["complete"] else "stopped",
             eta_s=prev.get("eta_s", p["eta_s"]) if running else p["eta_s"], credits_projected=prev.get("credits_projected"),
             **{k: prev.get(k, 0) for k in ("billed_gpu_seconds", "wall_s", "credits_so_far")},
             workers=prev.get("workers", {}) if running else {}, updated_s_ago=round(now() - prev.get("t", now()), 1))
    if a.chunks:
        p["chunks"] = {st.name: {c: "done" if c in S.done_ids(st.name) else f"fail x{len(S.fails(st.name, c))}"
                                 if S.fails(st.name, c) else "todo" for c in S.selected(st)} for st in S.job.stages}
    if a.json:
        return print(json.dumps(p, sort_keys=True)) or 0
    print(f"{p['job']}  {p['state']}  {p['percent']}%  eta {fmt_s(p['eta_s'])}  updated {fmt_s(p['updated_s_ago'])} ago")
    for n, s in p["stages"].items():
        print(f"  {n:<12} {s['kind']:<10} {s['done_units']}/{s['total_units']} {s['unit']}  chunks {s['done_chunks']}/"
              f"{s['total_chunks']}  running {s['running']}  failed {s['failed_chunks']}  eta {fmt_s(s['eta_s'])}")
    if p["workers"]:
        print("  gpus: " + " | ".join(f"{g} {w.get('item', w.get('state'))}" for g, w in sorted(p["workers"].items())))
    if p["quarantined"]:
        print(f"  quarantined gpus: {', '.join(p['quarantined'])}")
    print(f"  credits: {p['credits_so_far']:.0f} so far" + (f", ~{p['credits_projected']:.0f} projected" if running
          and p["credits_projected"] is not None else "") + f" ({len(p['gpus'])} GPUs); retries {p['retries']}")
    for n, cs in (p.get("chunks") or {}).items():
        print(f"  {n}: " + " ".join(f"{c}={v}" for c, v in cs.items()))
    return 0


def cmd_report(a):
    S = State(a.state)
    p = read_json(S.p("progress.json"), {})
    q = summarize(S, base={k: p.get(k, 0) for k in ("billed_gpu_seconds", "wall_s")})
    evs = read_jsonl(S.p("events.jsonl"))
    match = lambda e, kinds, spec: e["ev"] in kinds and (spec is None or bool(e.get("spec")) == spec)
    n = lambda kind, spec=None: sum(1 for e in evs if match(e, (kind,), spec))
    secs = lambda kinds, spec=None: round(sum(e.get("seconds", 0) for e in evs if match(e, kinds, spec)), 1)
    busy, billed = q["gpu_seconds_busy"] + secs(("chunk_superseded", "chunk_abandoned")), q["billed_gpu_seconds"]
    r = dict(job=S.job.name, complete=q["complete"], percent=q["percent"], wall_s=q["wall_s"], runs=n("run_start"),
             gpus=p.get("gpus", []), gpu_seconds_busy=round(busy, 1), billed_gpu_seconds=billed,
             busy_pct=round(100 * busy / billed, 1) if billed else None, idle_gpu_seconds=round(max(0.0, billed - busy), 1),
             credits=round(billed * S.job.rate, 1), retries=q["retries"], quarantined=q["quarantined"],
             worker_deaths=n("worker_died"), leases_stolen=n("lease_stolen"), duplicates=n("chunk_duplicate"),
             speculative=n("chunk_start", True), speculative_won=n("chunk_done", True),
             speculative_gpu_seconds=secs(("chunk_done", "chunk_superseded"), True),
             superseded_gpu_seconds=secs(("chunk_superseded",)),
             stages={k: {x: s[x] for x in ("done_units", "total_units", "done_chunks", "total_chunks", "failed_chunks")}
                     for k, s in q["stages"].items()})
    if a.json:
        return print(json.dumps(r, sort_keys=True)) or 0
    print(f"GPUJOB report {r['job']} {'complete' if r['complete'] else 'INCOMPLETE ' + str(r['percent']) + '%'} "
          f"wall {fmt_s(r['wall_s'])} over {r['runs']} run(s); GPU busy {fmt_s(busy)} of {fmt_s(billed)} billed "
          f"({r['busy_pct']}% busy, {fmt_s(r['idle_gpu_seconds'])} idle); {r['credits']:.0f} credits; retries {r['retries']}; "
          f"worker deaths {r['worker_deaths']}; speculative {r['speculative']} ({r['speculative_won']} won, "
          f"{fmt_s(r['speculative_gpu_seconds'])} GPU); quarantined {','.join(r['quarantined']) or 'none'}")
    return 0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- estimate
def wall_estimate(job, chunk_secs, seq_secs, gpus):
    """Wall seconds on `gpus` GPUs. A sequential stage holds one GPU; chunk stages stream behind it."""
    ts, n = sum(seq_secs.values()), sum(len(s.chunks) for s in job.stages if s.kind == "chunks")
    work = sum(chunk_secs[s.name] * len(s.chunks) for s in job.stages if s.kind == "chunks")
    c = max([chunk_secs[s.name] for s in job.stages if s.kind == "chunks"] or [0])
    if not ts:
        return -(-n // gpus) * (work / n if n else 0)
    if gpus == 1:
        return ts + work
    return ts + c if work / (gpus - 1) <= ts else ts + (work - (gpus - 1) * ts) / gpus + c / 2


def cmd_estimate(a):
    job = Job.load(a.job)
    root = os.path.abspath(a.state or os.path.join(job.workdir, ".gpujob", job.name))
    err = lambda msg, rc: print(f"gpujob estimate: {msg}", file=sys.stderr) or rc
    if a.pilot:  # first, middle and last chunk of each independent chunk stage, one per GPU: committed, not wasted
        picks = list(dict.fromkeys(f"{s.name}:{ids[i]}" for s in job.stages if s.kind == "chunks" and not s.after
                                   for ids in [list(s.chunks)] for i in (0, len(ids) // 2, -1)))
        if not picks:
            return err("--pilot needs a chunk stage without `after`", 2)
        gpus = detect_gpus(job.spec.get("gpus"), None)[:len(picks)]
        r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, ME, "run", a.job, "--state", root, "--gpus", ",".join(gpus), "--only",
                            ",".join(picks)], stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                           env=dict(os.environ, GPUJOB_SPECULATE="0"))  # measure each chunk's own time
        if r.returncode:
            return err(f"pilot failed (exit {r.returncode}); see status {root}", 1)
    S = State(root, job) if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(root, "chunks")) else None
    per = {"mean": {}, "low": {}, "high": {}}  # chunk seconds per stage: average, cheapest, dearest
    seq_secs = {}
    for s in job.stages:
        if s.kind == "chunks":
            n = int(s.d.get("chunk", 1))
            rates = [d["seconds"] / (s.chunks[c][1] - s.chunks[c][0] + 1) for c in (S.done_ids(s.name) if S else [])
                     for d in [S.done(s.name, c)] if d and c in s.chunks]  # seconds per frame
            if a.pilot_seconds or not rates:
                v = a.pilot_seconds or s.d.get("est_chunk_seconds")
                if v is None:
                    return err(f"no time for {s.name}: pass --pilot-seconds or --pilot", 2)
                rates = [float(v) / n]
            for k, f in (("mean", statistics.mean), ("low", min), ("high", max)):
                per[k][s.name] = f(rates) * n
        else:
            v = s.d.get("est_seconds") or s.d.get("est_unit_seconds", 0) * s.total_units or a.seq_seconds
            if not v:
                return err(f"stage {s.name} needs est_seconds/est_unit_seconds or --seq-seconds", 2)
            seq_secs[s.name] = float(v)
    gpu_s = {k: sum(cs[s.name] * len(s.chunks) for s in job.stages if s.kind == "chunks") + sum(seq_secs.values())
             for k, cs in per.items()}
    cr = lambda x: round(x * job.rate)
    rows = []
    for m, g in [(1, 1), (1, 2), (1, 4), (2, 4), (4, 4)]:  # 4 GPUs: the largest plan cap
        w = {k: wall_estimate(job, cs, seq_secs, m * g) for k, cs in per.items()}  # billed; placing isn't
        rows.append(dict(machines=m, gpus_per_machine=g, wall_s=round(w["mean"] + (a.startup_seconds if m > 1 else 0), 1),
                         credits=cr(w["mean"] * m * g), credits_low=cr(w["low"] * m * g), credits_high=cr(w["high"] * m * g)))
    res = dict(job=job.name, gpu_seconds=round(gpu_s["mean"], 1), gpu_seconds_low=round(gpu_s["low"], 1),
               gpu_seconds_high=round(gpu_s["high"], 1), credits_min=cr(gpu_s["mean"]), options=rows,
               chunk_seconds=per["mean"], chunk_seconds_range=[per["low"], per["high"]], seq_seconds=seq_secs,
               credits_per_gpu_minute=job.rate * 60)
    if a.json:
        return print(json.dumps(res, sort_keys=True)) or 0
    print(f"GPUJOB estimate {job.name}: {fmt_s(gpu_s['mean'])} of GPU work (range {fmt_s(gpu_s['low'])}-"
          f"{fmt_s(gpu_s['high'])}; ~{cr(gpu_s['mean'])} credits, {cr(gpu_s['low'])}-{cr(gpu_s['high'])} at "
          f"{job.rate * 60:g} credits/GPU-min, no idle)")
    for r in rows:
        print(f"  {r['machines']} machine x {r['gpus_per_machine']} GPU: wall ~{fmt_s(r['wall_s'])}  ~{r['credits']} credits "
              f"({r['credits_low']}-{r['credits_high']})"
              + (f"  (wall includes {fmt_s(a.startup_seconds)} to place extra machines)" if r["machines"] > 1 else ""))
    return 0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- manifest, harvest
def manifest(S, after=0.0, limit=None):
    """What was committed after `after`, oldest first, at most `limit` entries: ({name: {"out": rel, "chunks":
    {key: record}}}, next cursor, {stage: [done ids]}). Entries: .done records of harvested stages, and for
    sequential stages each unit file ("u:<file>") and the newest checkpoint ("<stage>#ckpt", "c:<file>@<mtime>")."""
    ents, done = [], {}

    def filerec(path, base):
        return {"outputs": [{"path": os.path.relpath(path, base), "bytes": os.path.getsize(path),
                             "sha256": sha256_file(path)}]}
    for st in S.job.stages:
        ids = S.done_ids(st.name)
        done[st.name] = sorted(ids)
        for cid in ids if st.harvest else []:
            d = S.done(st.name, cid) or {}
            if d.get("t", 0) > after:
                ents.append((d["t"], st.name, st.out_rel, cid, lambda d=d: d))
        if st.kind == "sequential":
            for f in unit_files(st.out, st.unit_glob):
                if os.path.getmtime(f) > after:
                    ents.append((os.path.getmtime(f), st.name, st.out_rel, "u:" + os.path.basename(f),
                                 lambda f=f, st=st: filerec(f, st.out)))
            for f in sorted(unit_files(S.job.workdir, st.checkpoint), key=os.path.getmtime)[-1:] if st.checkpoint else []:
                if os.path.getmtime(f) > after:
                    ents.append((os.path.getmtime(f), st.name + "#ckpt", ".",
                                 f"c:{os.path.relpath(f, S.job.workdir)}@{os.path.getmtime(f)}",
                                 lambda f=f: filerec(f, S.job.workdir)))
    ents.sort(key=lambda e: e[0])
    full = bool(limit) and len(ents) > limit
    # a full page advances only past entries older than the first one left out (two commits can share a time)
    nxt = max([e[0] for e in ents[:limit] if e[0] < ents[limit][0]], default=after) if full else None
    ents, m = ents[:limit] if limit else ents, {}
    for t, name, out_rel, key, rec in ents:
        r = quiet(rec)  # None: replaced between listing and hashing; the next poll sees the new file
        if r is not None:
            m.setdefault(name, {"out": out_rel, "chunks": {}})["chunks"][key] = {
                "outputs": r.get("outputs", []), "gpu": r.get("gpu"), "seconds": r.get("seconds")}
    # a file renamed into place keeps its older write time, so re-offer the last 30 s (harvest skips known keys)
    cursor = nxt if full else min(ents[-1][0] if ents else after, max(after, now() - 30))
    return m, cursor, done


def harvest_into(man, fetch, dest, staging, log=print):
    """Copy committed outputs into dest: fetch(out_rel, rel, tmp) into staging, check sha256, move into place if
    absent. dest/.gpujob-harvest.json lists each harvested key once (first copy wins). Returns (new, failed)."""
    mpath = os.path.join(dest, ".gpujob-harvest.json")
    have, new, fails = read_json(mpath, {}), 0, 0
    for sname, info in man.items():
        got = have.setdefault(sname, {})
        for cid, rec in sorted(info["chunks"].items()):
            if cid in got:
                continue
            ok = True
            for o in rec["outputs"]:
                final = os.path.join(dest, info["out"], o["path"])
                if os.path.isfile(final) and os.path.getsize(final) == o["bytes"] and sha256_file(final) == o["sha256"]:
                    continue
                tmp = os.path.join(staging, info["out"], o["path"])
                os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(tmp), exist_ok=True)
                for attempt in range(3):
                    fetch(info["out"], o["path"], tmp)
                    if os.path.isfile(tmp) and sha256_file(tmp) == o["sha256"]:
                        break
                    log(f"GPUJOB event harvest_hash_mismatch {sname}:{cid} {o['path']} try={attempt + 1}")
                else:
                    ok, fails = False, fails + 1
                    break
                os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(final), exist_ok=True)
                os.replace(tmp, final)
                fsync_dir(os.path.dirname(final))
            if ok:
                got[cid], new = {"outputs": rec["outputs"], "gpu": rec.get("gpu"), "t": now()}, new + 1
    write_json(mpath, have)
    return new, fails


def cmd_harvest(a):
    S, dest = State(a.state), os.path.abspath(a.to)
    new, _ = harvest_into(manifest(S)[0], lambda o, rel, tmp: shutil.copyfile(os.path.join(S.job.workdir, o, rel), tmp),
                          dest, os.path.join(dest, ".gpujob-staging", "local"))
    out(f"GPUJOB harvest {new} new chunk(s) into {dest}")
    return 0


def cmd_manifest(a):
    S = State(a.state)
    p = read_json(S.p("progress.json"), {})
    m, cursor, done = manifest(S, a.after, a.limit)
    print(json.dumps({"manifest": m, "cursor": cursor, "done": done, "progress": {k: p.get(k) for k in
                      ("percent", "state", "eta_s", "billed_gpu_seconds", "gpu_seconds_busy", "credits_so_far")}}))
    return 0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- cli
B = "store_true"
CLI = {  # sub-command: (help, [(flag, type or action, help, default)])
    "run": ("run (or resume) a job on this machine's GPUs", [
        ("job",), ("--state",), ("--gpus", str, "comma list of GPU indices (default: job 'gpus', else all)"),
        ("--only", str, "chunk ids (stage:id or id), comma/space separated, or @file"),
        ("--stages", str, "comma list of stage names to run"), ("--partition", str, "i/n: only slice i of n"),
        ("--unquarantine", B, "give quarantined GPUs another chance")]),
    "_worker": (None, [("state",), ("gpu",)]),
    "status": ("progress of a running or stopped job", [("state",), ("--json", B, "one small JSON object"),
                                                        ("--chunks", B, "per-chunk detail (large)")]),
    "estimate": ("GPU time, wall and credits for 1-4 GPUs and 2-4 machines", [
        ("job",), ("--pilot-seconds", float, "seconds one chunk takes on one GPU"),
        ("--pilot", B, "render first, middle and last chunk for real, in parallel (kept)"),
        ("--seq-seconds", float, "seconds a sequential stage takes"), ("--state",), ("--json", B, ""),
        ("--startup-seconds", float, "wall to place extra machines (unbilled)", 300.0)]),
    "report": ("after: wall, GPU-seconds, busy %%, credits, retries", [("state",), ("--json", B, "")]),
    "harvest": ("copy committed outputs (sha256-verified) into a folder", [("state",), ("--to", str, "folder")]),
    "manifest": (None, [("state",), ("--after", float, "only what was committed after this cursor", 0.0),
                        ("--limit", int, "at most this many entries per call", 200)]),
}


def main(argv=None, cli=CLI, handlers=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=os.path.basename(sys.argv[0]), description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    sp = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    for name, (hlp, args) in cli.items():
        p = sp.add_parser(name, **({"help": hlp} if hlp else {}))
        for flag, kind, *rest in [x + (str,) if len(x) == 1 else x for x in args]:
            kw = {"action": kind} if kind in (B, "append") else {"type": kind}
            kw.update({k: v for k, v in zip(("help", "default"), rest) if v or k == "default"})
            p.add_argument(flag, **kw)
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    if a.cmd == "harvest" and not a.to:
        ap.error("harvest needs --to")
    return dict({"run": cmd_run, "_worker": lambda a: Worker(State(a.state), a.gpu).main(), "status": cmd_status,
                 "estimate": cmd_estimate, "report": cmd_report, "harvest": cmd_harvest, "manifest": cmd_manifest},
                **(handlers or {}))[a.cmd](a)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

---
name: gpu-machines
description: Run heavy or CUDA-only work on Voyager GPUs (remote machines) - long renders, simulations, training, model inference, live previews - and reconnect to, snapshot, pause or resume that work. Not for quick local work.
---

Voyager GPUs are remote machines for work this computer can't do well: long Blender or Unreal renders,
simulations, training, model inference, CUDA-only tools, a private running service. Arbitrary code,
packages and up to the plan's GPU limit (Creator 2, Ultra and GigaMax 4) are fine. The agent,
editable source, conversation and timeline stay local; a machine holds compute, selected inputs,
caches and intermediates. A fixed operation Voyager already offers (a generation, a local export) is
usually simpler without one. Follow the Voyager GPUs preference in your instructions for when to
ask, and talk to the user about outcomes, time and credits, not machines, IDs or paths.

Every step is a `voyager machine <verb>` command (`--help` lists flags), and in the app a
`machine_<verb>` tool where one exists. Give each mutation a stable `requestId` and reuse it after an
uncertain answer; it never runs twice.

## Lifecycle

1. **offers**: cards, VRAM, graphics/NVENC and `credits_per_minute` for the GPU count asked (the
   whole machine). Estimate credits as minutes × that rate. With no card or requirement given,
   lease uses the default card; ask by `vramMin`, `graphics` or `nvenc` when the work needs them.
2. **lease**: returns at once while the machine starts (a minute or more cold). Keep working
   locally; `wait` when you need it. `list` finds machines you already have, including after a
   lost context; closing Voyager does not release them.
3. **sync push**: selected paths, hash-checked, unchanged files skipped. Keep big intermediates,
   weights and caches on the machine.
4. **exec**: argv (or `--shell`), usually `--detach`. Then `job status`, `logs` with `tailBytes`,
   `job wait` with a short timeout, `cancel`. A detached job is tracked and wakes the conversation
   when it ends, so you can end the turn once its first log lines look right. Check the job's
   state and exit code, not just the call's success.
5. **inspect / sync pull / ingest**: `inspect` samples frames and probes a video on the machine
   before you download it. Package outputs there (encode frames, archive many files), pull the
   smallest useful thing, and `ingest` a take to verify, present and optionally place it.
6. **release** when the last job is done and outputs are home or snapshotted. Check it reports
   released. `usage` shows a machine's spend so far.

Also there: `port` (a private HTTPS preview of a service; its token is a credential, not a share
link), `snapshot`, `pause`, `resume` and `fork`; see [recovery](references/recovery.md).

## Shape the machine

| Need                                              | Ask for                                                                               |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A specific card or capability                     | `gpu` from offers, or `vramMin` / `graphics` / `nvenc`                                |
| More GPUs                                         | `gpus`, up to the plan limit; one process sees them all                               |
| CPU-heavy steps (shader compiles, decoding, sims) | `cpu`, up to 256 cores                                                                |
| Large scenes, datasets or models in memory        | `ramGib`, up to 2048                                                                  |
| Tools and versions                                | `images` lists images and their tools; `pip`/`apt` installs work too                  |
| Installs and caches that outlive a machine        | `volume` (mounted at `/persist`), or a `disk` snapshot to `fork` from                 |
| Lifetime                                          | `ttlS` hard limit; `idleS` releases an idle machine                                   |
| A long job                                        | exec `timeoutS` for a job you expect to run for hours                                 |
| API keys or tokens                                | exec `env`; keep them out of pushed files and logs                                    |
| No internet                                       | `network.mode: "blocked"`                                                             |
| A spend cap                                       | `budgetUsd`, only when the user asks for one; otherwise the workspace's credits apply |

## Recipes and helpers

The bundled scripts are a strong default, not the only route; write your own when the work needs it.

- [Blender](references/blender.md): pack a scene, render on every GPU with resume and progress
  lines, encode on the machine and finalize the result.
- [Chunked jobs and fan-out](references/fanout.md): `gpujob.py` keeps every GPU busy on frames,
  tiles or shots with retries and resume; `gpujob_fanout.py` spreads one job over several machines.
- [Recovery and preservation](references/recovery.md): reconnecting, snapshots, pause and resume,
  and what each one actually keeps.

When the work is done, present the accepted result, say what it cost in credits, and release.
